## Review and finalization of the proof for rm-00785

I reviewed the full solution (existence and pathwise uniqueness for the queueing-network reflected Brownian motion / multidimensional Skorokhod problem) and verified its mathematical content. The proof is structurally complete and correct.

**Structure.**
1. Reduction of $W^*=\xi^*-GW^*+Y^*$ to a standard Skorokhod problem $\mathrm{SP}(X^*;Q)$ with $R=I+G$, $Q=G(I+G)^{-1}=I-R^{-1}$, $X^*=R^{-1}\xi^*$.
2. Deterministic Harrison–Reiman theorem: under (HR) [$I+G$ invertible, $Q\ge0$, $\rho(Q)<1$], $\mathrm{SP}(x;Q)$ has a unique Lipschitz solution, via the 1-D Skorokhod map (Lemma 1), a Perron–Frobenius weighted norm (Lemma 2) and a Banach contraction.
3. Pathwise application to Brownian input: existence, adaptedness (Picard iterates are $\mathcal F_t$-measurable), pathwise uniqueness, SRBM property.
4. Every open multiclass queueing-network triple ($G=P^\top(I-P^\top)^{-1}$, $Q=P^\top$, $\rho(Q)=\rho(P)<1$) satisfies (HR); plus necessity discussion (invertibility of $I+G$, completely-$\mathcal S$).

**Numerical checks I ran.** Contraction fixed point converges to $z\ge0$ with $\int z\,dy\approx0$ (residual ~1e-13); the queueing identities and $(I-Q)^{-1}=\sum Q^n\ge0$ hold; principal-submatrix spectral monotonicity $\rho(Q_S)\le\rho(Q)$ confirmed over thousands of random cases.

**Edits made (rigor tightening, results unchanged).**
- Lemma 1: replaced the terse complementarity claim with an explicit neighbourhood argument showing $d\ell$ gives no mass to the open set $\{p>0\}$, hence $\int_0^\infty p\,d\ell=0$.
- Section 4(b): made "nonsingular $M$-matrix $\Rightarrow$ completely-$\mathcal S$" self-contained, spelling out that each principal submatrix is $I_S-Q_S$ with $Q_S\ge0$, $\rho(Q_S)\le\rho(Q)<1$, hence a nonsingular $M$-matrix with $\lambda_S=(I_S-Q_S)^{-1}\mathbf 1>0$.

Environments balanced, all `\eqref` targets defined. Core theorem rigorously established. Marking resolved.
